title: Corchea: Paper-Based Microfluidic Device
author: Gonzalo Vidal-Peña
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vtwe6pe
materials: Put the acrylic paper sandwich in the lid of the hardware.

steps.title: Draw device layout
steps.instruction: Draw the borders of the microfluidic device and the future channels on Whatman #1 filter paper.

steps.title: Cut device outline
steps.instruction: Cut the drawn borders to separate the device shape from the surrounding paper.

steps.title: Apply wax barriers
steps.instruction: Fill all regions where fluid should not pass with wax crayons, creating hydrophobic barriers.

steps.title: Melt wax barriers
steps.instruction: Place the wax‑filled paper in a regular oven set to 100 °C for 140 seconds, then remove it and allow the wax to solidify, ensuring it fully penetrates the paper thickness.

steps.title: Assemble acrylic sandwich
steps.instruction: Place the paper between two acrylic sheets; optionally apply tape around the edges to improve impermeability.

steps.title: Connect paper ends
steps.instruction: Insert the paper ends into the source reservoir and close the device; a tip box can be used as a support point for the ends.

steps.title: Secure sandwich and add filter
steps.instruction: Insert the paper‑acrylic sandwich into a clip to maintain pressure and place a filter on top of the assembly.

steps.title: Introduce bacteria
steps.instruction: Add your chosen bacteria directly into the channels, or first culture bacteria on paper discs and then place the discs into the channels.

steps.title: Incubate and image
steps.instruction: Place the assembled device in an incubator for the desired incubation time, then acquire results using a FluoPi low‑cost open‑access transilluminator.
